titleStmt.title: The Significance of Advanced Mathematics in Secondary and Higher Education
titleStmt.author: Bhasin

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: The Significance of Advanced Mathematics in Secondary and Higher Education

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The exploration of higher-level mathematics during secondary education or at the university level presents a vast array of advantages that reach far beyond the realm of mathematics alone.

span.label: benefits of advanced mathematics education
span.quote: Learning advanced mathematics in high school or college offers a myriad of benefits to students in academic, personal, and professional pursuits as it presents them with the opportunity to engage in critical, abstract, and logical thinking.

span.label: review
span.quote: The present study delves into the advantages of learning advanced mathematics in high school or college.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Working through complex problems forces decomposition and strategy-building, and this reasoning process is what drives the cognitive and brain development the paper claims
span.quote: This process of reasoning and problem-solving fosters brain development and elevates overall cognitive skills.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Girls withhold questions out of shyness, unresolved doubts accumulate, they infer they cannot understand mathematics, and confidence falls
span.quote: Consequently, when girls feel bashful and refrain from asking questions, they may start believing that they lack the ability to comprehend math, resulting in a loss of self-confidence.

span.label: The paper's central term is never defined, only exemplified by naming school subjects, so every conclusion about it is a conclusion about whichever courses carry those names.
span.note: what this limits: any claim in this paper about 'advanced mathematics': the term is never defined, and the closest the paper comes is naming calculus, linear algebra and statistics as its content
span.quote: It builds a solid foundation in quantitative analysis through calculus, linear algebra, and statistics

span.label: Three results on the same question, by the same author, point in different directions and are printed one after another without being reconciled.
span.note: what this limits: the direction of the gender difference reported here: within one paragraph boys' mean scores are said to surpass girls' (Mansory, 2010) and girls are said to perform generally better (Mansory, 2007), with no reconciliation offered
span.quote: According to a survey conducted on 3rd-grade students in Afghanistan (Mansory, 2000), girls' math achievements surpassed boys in certain homeschools, though results might differ in formal schools. Disparities in mathematics performance may be linked to variations in specific school factors. Nevertheless, in governmental schools from grades 3 to 6, both male and female pupils attained superior results in language compared to mathematics. Notably, boys' mean scores in math surpassed those of girls (Mansory, 2010). Additionally, in grades 3-6, the representation of female learners was inferior to that of male learners, while their academic achievements varied. Another investigation focusing on grades 1-9 in Afghanistan uncovered that girls generally demonstrated superior performance, resulting in fewer conditional passes and reduced dropout rates when compared to their male counterparts (Mansory, 2007)

span.label: The mechanisms offered for the parental-background findings are the paper's own speculation, marked as such by its hedges, and are stated in the same breath as the findings.
span.note: what this limits: the parental-background explanations: the paper attributes better arithmetic to shopkeeper fathers 'potentially due to practical learning experiences' and lower achievement to educated fathers 'possibly due to' busy schedules -- both hedged, neither tested
span.quote: children whose fathers possess Islamic education tend to excel in reading, and those with shopkeeper fathers demonstrate better arithmetic skills, potentially due to practical learning experiences in their fathers' shops. On the other hand, children with educated fathers may experience lower achievements, possibly due to their fathers

span.label: The whole of the paper's stated method is that it delves into the advantages; no search, no inclusion criteria and no data are described.
span.note: what this limits: this paper as a review: its only statement of what was done is that it delves into the advantages of learning advanced mathematics, with no search or selection criteria given
span.quote: The present study delves into the advantages of learning advanced mathematics in high school or college

span.label: advanced mathematics
span.quote: Advanced mathematics imparts students with a profound grasp of numerical concepts and their real-world applications

span.label: quantitative literacy
span.quote: Proficiency in quantitative literacy proves crucial in fields like finance, economics, data analysis, and scientific research

span.label: mathematical achievement
span.quote: even though there are no substantial gender-based variances in mathematical achievement

span.label: self-confidence
span.quote: it is crucial to recognize that excessive self-confidence can also pose challenges for learners

span.label: advanced mathematics - NEVER DEFINED, ONLY EXEMPLIFIED: given as the content of calculus, linear algebra and statistics rather than by any property that would decide a borderline case
span.quote: It builds a solid foundation in quantitative analysis through calculus, linear algebra, and statistics

span.label: mathematical achievement vs confidence - STATED TO COME APART: girls report lower confidence while the paper reports no substantial gender difference in achievement itself
span.quote: studies have indicated that young females frequently manifest reduced confidence in their mathematical aptitude when compared to males, even though there are no substantial gender-based variances in mathematical achievement

span.label: self-confidence - BOUNDED ON BOTH SIDES: too little is treated as a barrier and too much as its own difficulty, so the paper does not treat more confidence as simply better
span.quote: it is crucial to recognize that excessive self-confidence can also pose challenges for learners, as overly confident students may struggle when confronted with difficult situations

span.label: qualifies → Dweck (2000)
span.note: differs in: WHETHER MORE CONFIDENCE IS ALWAYS BETTER. The paper treats low confidence as a barrier and then bounds the other end: 'EXCESSIVE SELF-CONFIDENCE CAN ALSO POSE CHALLENGES FOR LEARNERS, as overly confident students MAY STRUGGLE WHEN CONFRONTED WITH DIFFICULT SITUATIONS.' A variable bounded on both sides has no direction of improvement, so an intervention that raises it cannot be evaluated without knowing where a learner started
span.quote: However, it is crucial to recognize that excessive self-confidence can also pose challenges for learners, as overly confident students may struggle when confronted with difficult situations (Dweck, 2000).

span.label: builds-on → Gray (1996)
span.note: differs in: THE POPULATION THE FINDING IS SCOPED TO, WHICH THE SENTENCE STATES TWICE. 'RESEARCH IN THE US shows that students who receive parental support in mathematical activities perform better, IRRESPECTIVE OF GENDER' - a country in the subject and a gender-independence claim in the predicate. Both are conditions of the result and both are the kind of clause a downstream citation drops
span.quote: Research in the US shows that students who receive parental support in mathematical activities perform better, irrespective of gender (Gray, 1996).

span.label: qualifies → Mushtaq (2013)
span.note: differs in: WHERE THE QUESTION IS ASKED. Immediately after the gender-independent US result: 'HOWEVER, IN CERTAIN SOCIETIES SUCH AS AFGHANISTAN, girls' math performance can be affected by multiple factors, including parental background and encouragement, CULTURAL IMPACTS, socioeconomic circumstances, and self-assurance.' The same question about the same relation gets different answers in two countries, and the two sentences sit adjacent with only a 'however' between them
span.quote: However, in certain societies such as Afghanistan, girls' math performance can be affected by multiple factors, including parental background and encouragement, cultural impacts, socioeconomic circumstances, and self-assurance (Mushtaq, 2013).

span.label: self-confidence —distinct-from→ mathematical achievement
span.quote: studies have indicated that young females frequently manifest reduced confidence in their mathematical aptitude when compared to males, even though there are no substantial gender-based variances in mathematical achievement

span.label: The article concludes that studying higher-level mathematics yields benefits well beyond mathematics itself, across cognitive, quantitative, logical and vocational domains.
span.quote: The exploration of higher-level mathematics during secondary education or at the university level presents a vast array of advantages that reach far beyond the realm of mathematics alone.

span.label: It claims that advanced mathematics works by forcing students into critical, abstract and logical thinking.
span.quote: Advanced mathematics challenges students to engage in critical, abstract, and logical thinking.

span.label: It reports that young women show lower confidence in their mathematical ability than young men even where achievement does not differ by gender.
span.quote: Curiously, studies have indicated that young females frequently manifest reduced confidence in their mathematical aptitude when compared to males, even though there are no substantial gender-based variances in mathematical achievement (Watt, 2007).

span.label: It reports that cooperative rather than competitive classroom activity is more advantageous for girls' mathematics learning.
span.quote: Studies indicate that collaborative activities are more beneficial for female students (Fennema, 1996).

span.label: It reports that parental support in mathematical activity is associated with better student performance regardless of gender.
span.quote: Research in the US shows that students who receive parental support in mathematical activities perform better, irrespective of gender (Gray, 1996).

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.52783/eel.v13i3.493.
